You are working on a YouTube video editing pipeline (Windows, ffmpeg-based, HyperFrames for motion graphics). Main compositing script:

C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\scripts\composite_full.py

Read it in full first — do not rely on any assumed prior state, read the actual current file. Also read C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\tools\video-use\helpers\zoom_filter.py's docstring for this project's hard-won ffmpeg gotchas (eval=frame requirements for scale/pad w/h AND x/y, no clip() in ffmpeg eval, parenthesization of round() expressions, alpha-webm decode requiring explicit -c:v libvpx-vp9) before writing any filter expressions — these have caused real, shipped bugs in this exact file before.

## Background / current state

`build_webcam_primary()` implements a "hero stage" webcam_primary layout: a retrowave animated background, the webcam enlarged to ~1306x980 ("HERO" size) centered on the 1920x1080 canvas, and a neon-glow border loop scaled to hug the webcam's box. For two specific EDL ranges that carry a motion-graphic overlay (range 5 = `slot_bank_stat`, range 18 = `slot_codely_reveal` + `slot_tag_subscribe`), the webcam currently animates from HERO size down to the STANDARD PIP size (576x432, `PIP_W`/`PIP_H`) tucked into a bottom-right corner while the graphic plays, then grows back. This shrink/grow uses a 0.5s eased blend factor `u` (see `_shrink_u_expr`/`_hero_transform`) and the neon border is currently only shown at the two SETTLED endpoints (hero scale, or native-1:1-scale translated to the corner) — hidden entirely during the actual transition.

Also present: `TRANSITION_BOUNDARIES` in `main()` builds smooth xfade/acrossfade crossfades at 5 specific webcam_primary↔screen_primary layout-change boundaries (6→7, 11→12, 13→14, 17→18, 20→21) — hard cuts everywhere else. `OVERLAYS` dict has mic-indicator graphics (`slot_mic_indicator_1`/`slot_mic_indicator_2`) only on ranges 39 and 40.

## New requirements from the user (verbatim, then broken down)

> "when we are in full mode and there's [motion] graphics to appear over top of the retro wave BG, I don't want to descale the webcam down to the same size that we normally have it when it's over top of a screen recording. I kinda just want to scale it down by thirty to forty percent and move the webcam to the other side of the screen. So that way the motion graphic can appear directly horizontal to the webcam. I want the movement and the transition of the webcam moving to be smooth. I also want the neon glow border around the webcam to scale down or up with the webcam video in correspondence to the context of the video. This logic applies throughout all situations, not just in the full mode, but when we're transitioning from the screen recording and then going back and forth between screen recording and full webcam mode. I don't want any sharp cutoffs or transitions at all. Everything needs to flow smoothly and properly keyframed."

Broken down into concrete tasks:

### 1. Redesign the dynamic shrink-aside target state (ranges 5 and 18)

Instead of shrinking to the standard 576x432 PIP size in a corner, shrink to **60-70% of HERO size** (i.e. a 30-40% reduction, not a ~44% *of-hero-height* reduction down to the tiny PIP) and **move it to whichever side of the screen is clear of that graphic's own content** (inspect each graphic's actual rendered content bounding box across its FULL timeline — not just its opening frame, per a lesson already learned once in this project, see the existing `SHRINK_CORNER` comment in the file for the prior investigation) so the graphic and the shrunk webcam sit side-by-side, roughly horizontally aligned, rather than the graphic sprawling behind a tiny corner PIP. Pick the exact scale factor within the 60-70%-of-hero range and the exact resting position based on what actually looks balanced against each graphic's real content — verify by extracting frames and looking, not just by formula.

Do this per-range (or per-graphic, if range 18's two graphics — `slot_codely_reveal` then `slot_tag_subscribe` — would genuinely benefit from different resting positions; but prefer ONE consistent resting position per range if both graphics in that range are compatible with it, to avoid the webcam hopping sides mid-range, which the user didn't ask for and would itself look like an unwanted "sharp" change).

### 2. Neon border must scale continuously with the webcam, not just snap at the two endpoints

Currently the border is hidden during the shrink/grow transition itself (only shown at u<0.02 or u>0.98, i.e. only in the two settled states) — the code comment calls this "a deliberate simplification." The user now explicitly wants the border to visibly scale UP/DOWN in lockstep with the webcam at every point of the animation, not disappear and reappear. Redesign this to be continuous: the border should track the webcam's frame-varying size/position at every frame during the transition, matching the box the webcam currently occupies. You have working reference techniques already in this file for frame-varying scale (`eval=frame` on `scale`'s w/h) and frame-varying position (`overlay`'s x/y, which — per the existing code comment — DOES support a `t`-varying expression, unlike `pad`'s x/y which does NOT). Use the same "scale to the frame-varying box, then overlay onto a constant-size transparent canvas at the frame-varying absolute position" pattern already used for the webcam itself (see `_hero_transform` / the dynamic branch of `build_webcam_primary()`) to make the border ALSO continuously scale/reposition in lockstep — you'll likely want to scale the raw 1920x1080 border frame by a t-varying factor (interpolating between the hero scale `NEON_SCALE_HERO` and whatever new corner-state scale you land on) and center-overlay it onto the webcam's own current box center at every frame, analogous to how the webcam itself is handled. Verify the border visibly hugs the webcam's edge at multiple SAMPLED MID-TRANSITION frames (not just the two endpoints) — extract real frames during the shrink and during the grow-back and confirm the border tracks correctly, no lag, no mismatch, no popping.

### 3. Smooth, no sharp cutoffs "throughout all situations"

Interpret this primarily as: the redesigned shrink/grow/reposition animation (tasks 1-2) must itself be smoothly eased throughout (it already uses an eased `u` blend factor via `_shrink_u_expr` — carry that same discipline into the new design, don't introduce any instant jumps). Additionally, specifically check and fix this real edge case: **range 18 starts immediately after a screen_primary→webcam_primary crossfade transition (boundary 17→18), and range 18's first graphic (`slot_codely_reveal`) starts at `rel_start=0.05` — almost immediately.** Under the CURRENT design this means the webcam briefly flashes at full HERO size for a fraction of a second right as the scene-transition crossfade completes, then immediately shrinks — a "pop." Investigate whether this is actually visible (extract frames right at that boundary in the currently-cached `composited_draft.mp4` or a fresh render) and if so, fix it — e.g. by having the shrink-window logic treat a graphic that starts essentially at t=0 of the range as "already in the shrunk state from the range's very start" rather than animating a to full hero and immediately back down. Do NOT attempt to unify the screen_primary small-PIP layout and the webcam_primary hero layout into one continuously-tracked object across the hard layout-change boundaries themselves (that would require rearchitecting `build_screen_primary()` and the xfade transition logic too, which is out of scope) — the existing 0.4s xfade/acrossfade crossfade at those 5 boundaries already provides the "no sharp cutoff" behavior the user asked for at the screen↔webcam scene level; your job is to make sure the NEW shrink-aside redesign doesn't introduce a fresh pop immediately adjacent to those crossfades, not to rebuild the crossfade system itself. If you find OTHER similar adjacency issues (a graphic window starting/ending very close to a range boundary or another graphic), handle them with the same "would this look sharp/instant to a viewer" judgment.

### 4. Missing mic-indicator instances

The user says there were other moments where he's dictating to Claude via voice-to-text that don't currently have the mic/audio-visualizer overlay (`slot_mic_indicator_1`/`slot_mic_indicator_2` in `OVERLAYS`, currently only on ranges 39/40). Research: read `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\takes_packed.md` and/or the word-level transcripts in `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\transcripts\` cross-referenced against `edl.json`'s ranges 21-41 (the LIVE_BUILD beat) to find other live voice-dictation-into-Claude moments — look for the same signal that identified the existing two (a sustained stretch where he's speaking into a text input rather than narrating to camera; the existing `ZOOMS` entries at indices 21, 23, 26, 39, 40 target a right-panel input box, which is a strong hint — check whether 21/23/26 or any other un-flagged range is ALSO a live-dictation moment that should get a mic indicator but doesn't have one). For each new instance found, add an `OVERLAYS` entry reusing the existing `slot_mic_indicator_1`/`slot_mic_indicator_2` assets (don't build new ones — reuse, alternating or picking whichever fits, matching how the existing two are used) with an appropriate `rel_start`/`dur` window covering the actual dictation stretch (verify against the real transcript timestamps, not guesses). If you're not confident a candidate is genuinely a live-dictation-to-Claude moment (as opposed to just looking at a webpage or typing manually), don't add it — false positives are worse than a missed one; note anything ambiguous in your report instead of guessing.

## Deliverable: a new 60-second mockup video

Once the above is implemented and verified on the affected segments, build a new ~60-second demonstration cut (similar spirit to the earlier `first-video/edit/highlight_reel/` work — check that directory for the pattern used: short clips trimmed from the full composited output with brief fade in/out, concatenated, `-pix_fmt yuv420p` explicitly on every intermediate AND final encode to avoid a pix_fmt-mismatch playback bug that has already bitten this exact workflow once) showcasing:
- The redesigned shrink-aside behavior on ranges 5 and 18 (webcam at 60-70% hero size, moved to the side, graphic beside it, neon border scaling continuously through the transition)
- A webcam_primary↔screen_primary scene-transition crossfade
- Any newly-added mic-indicator instance(s), if you found and added any
- General hero-stage webcam_primary shots

**Render settings for this mockup specifically**: NO grain/flicker texture layer (skip `GRAIN_LOOP` compositing entirely for this build — the user has been going back and forth on whether they want it and the most recent instruction is "no static" for this mockup; don't delete the grain-compositing capability from the script permanently, just don't invoke it for this specific mockup output, e.g. via a temporary flag/parameter you can toggle, so the option to bring it back later isn't lost). Background scrim: a 25%-opacity black layer composited onto the raw retrowave background only (before the border/webcam are drawn on top — same layering principle already established in the file's grain-compositing fix, i.e. darken the background plate, never the webcam/border/graphic content itself) — bake this into the actual `build_webcam_primary()` output for this mockup (you can gate it behind the same toggle as the grain skip, or just hardcode a `SCRIM_OPACITY = 0.25` constant if that's simpler — your call, just make sure it's easy to find/adjust later since these values are still being iterated on).

Save the mockup to `C:\Users\edmem\OneDrive\Desktop\Video Projects\first-video\edit\mockups\demo_60s_v2.mp4`.

## Verification standard (read carefully — this matters)

This exact codebase has shipped "verified" work that turned out broken THREE separate times this session (a corner-PIP clipping bug, a grain layer covering the wrong region, and a false-positive bug report that was actually correct footage) — always because verification relied on checking only a couple of convenient timestamps (transition edges, opening frames) rather than dense sampling across a feature's FULL active window. For every new/changed behavior in this task:
- Sample MULTIPLE frames spread across the ENTIRE duration each new behavior is active (not just start/end) — for the shrink-aside redesign, sample at least 5-6 points across each graphic's full window including several mid-transition points during both the shrink and the grow-back.
- Extract real frames and actually look at them (describe what you see) rather than reasoning from the filter-graph expression alone.
- For anything involving alpha (the border, the graphics), decode with explicit `-c:v libvpx-vp9` and consider raw pixel sampling, not just ffprobe metadata.
- Confirm the final mockup decodes cleanly end-to-end (`ffmpeg -v error -i demo_60s_v2.mp4 -f null -`) and has uniform `pix_fmt` throughout (check every intermediate clip you concat, not just the final file — a per-clip mismatch can still silently break playback in some players even if ffmpeg's own null-decode doesn't complain).

## Deliverable / report

Modified `composite_full.py`, the rebuilt affected segments (`seg_05.mp4`, `seg_18.mp4`, and `composited_draft.mp4` if you choose to rebuild the full draft — your call whether that's needed for this task or whether segment-level + mockup-level verification is sufficient), the new `demo_60s_v2.mp4`, and a written report covering: exact scale factor and resting position chosen per range (with your reasoning from actual content inspection), how you made the neon border continuous through the transition (technique used, any gotchas hit), what you found/fixed for the range-18-adjacent-to-crossfade pop issue, what mic-indicator instances you found and added (or explicitly: found none, if that's the honest answer), and your dense verification results (describe the actual frames you looked at and what you saw) for every changed behavior. Do not ask clarifying questions — investigate and make the most reasonable, well-verified call on anything ambiguous, and document the decision.

294	def build_transition(seg_a: Path, seg_b: Path, out: Path, dur: float = XFADE_DUR, style: str = XFADE_STYLE) -> None:
295	    """Replace the hard cut between two already-built segments with a single
296	    merged clip: full seg_a, crossfading (video via xfade, audio in parallel
297	    via acrossfade) into full seg_b over `dur` seconds at the boundary. This
298	    one output clip REPLACES both seg_a and seg_b in the final concat list
299	    (its own duration is dur_a + dur_b - dur, since the overlapping tail/head
300	    now live once, blended, instead of twice). Both segments are already
301	    1920x1080/60fps/libx264/yuv420p/aac from the per-segment build step, so
302	    they're safe to feed straight into xfade/acrossfade as two -i inputs with
303	    no extra normalization needed.
304	
305	    `offset` (xfade's crossfade-start point, measured on seg_a's own
306	    timeline) is computed from seg_a's REAL encoded duration via ffprobe, not
307	    the EDL's nominal (end-start) -- see probe_duration()."""
308	    dur_a = probe_duration(seg_a)
309	    offset = dur_a - dur
310	    if offset < 0:
311	        print(f"FAILED: segment {seg_a} too short ({dur_a}s) for a {dur}s crossfade")
312	        sys.exit(1)
313	    filt = (
314	        f"[0:v][1:v]xfade=transition={style}:duration={dur}:offset={offset}[v];"
315	        f"[0:a][1:a]acrossfade=d={dur}[a]"
316	    )
317	    cmd = [
318	        FFMPEG, "-y",
319	        "-i", str(seg_a), "-i", str(seg_b),
320	        "-filter_complex", filt,
321	        "-map", "[v]", "-map", "[a]",
322	        "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast", "-crf", "18", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-c:a", "aac",
323	        str(out), "-loglevel", "error",
324	    ]
325	    run(cmd)

328	def zoom_filter(z: dict) -> str:
329	    # Supersample before zoompan (4x linear) so the crop window's pixel-rounded
330	    # position error shrinks proportionally at output res -- this is what
331	    # actually kills the end-of-ramp "vibration": zoompan rounds x/y to whole
332	    # *input* pixels each frame, and near the top of an ease-out curve many
333	    # consecutive frames have nearly-but-not-quite-identical zoom, so the
334	    # rounded crop position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution.
335	    # At 4x input res, that same 1px dither is a quarter-output-pixel: gone.
336	    # Rounding the zoom value itself to 4 decimals removes the sub-pixel
337	    # floating-point noise that was driving the dither in the first place.
338	    fps = 60
339	    rsf = z["rs"] * fps
340	    rdf = z["rd"] * fps
341	    cx, cy, Z = z["cx"] * 2, z["cy"] * 2, z["z"]  # cx/cy given in 1x source coords; input is prescaled 2x here
342	    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
343	    if z.get("out_rs") is not None:
344	        orsf = z["out_rs"] * fps
345	        ordf = z["out_rd"] * fps
346	        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
347	        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
348	    else:
349	        raw_zoom = f"1+({Z}-1)*{in_ease}"
350	    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw_zoom})*2000)/2000"
351	    x_expr = f"min(max({cx}-(iw/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,iw-iw/zoom)"
352	    y_expr = f"min(max({cy}-(ih/zoom/2)\\,0)\\,ih-ih/zoom)"
353	    zp = f"zoompan=z='{zoom_expr}':x='{x_expr}':y='{y_expr}':d=1:s=1920x1080:fps={fps}"
354	    return f"scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,{zp}"

386	def _shrink_u_expr(graphic_start: float, graphic_end: float, td: float) -> str:
387	    """0..1 blend factor for the webcam hero<->corner shrink-aside: 0 = full
388	    hero size/position, 1 = settled corner size/position. Ramps 0->1 (ease-out
389	    cubic) over `td` seconds ending exactly at graphic_start (so the shrink
390	    completes right as the graphic's own CRT entrance begins), holds at 1 for
391	    the graphic's whole window, then ramps back 1->0 over `td` seconds
392	    starting at graphic_end. Same min(ease_in,ease_out) shape as
393	    crt_transition_filter's s_expr, just inverted (0 at the edges instead of
394	    the middle is what we want here since 0 = hero/full-frame, matching s=1
395	    there -- so this reuses s_expr as-is: s=1 in the hold matches u=1 here)."""
396	    ws, we = graphic_start - td, graphic_end + td
397	    p_in = f"min(max((t-{ws})/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
398	    p_out = f"min(max(({we}-t)/{td}\\,0)\\,1)"
399	    ease_in = f"(1-pow(1-{p_in}\\,3))"
400	    ease_out = f"(1-pow(1-{p_out}\\,3))"
401	    return f"min({ease_in}\\,{ease_out})"

404	def _hero_transform(windows: list[tuple[float, float]], td: float = SHRINK_DUR) -> dict:
405	    """Piecewise scale(w,h)/position(x,y) expressions for the webcam feed,
406	    blending between the hero-stage size/position and the SHRINK_CORNER
407	    size/position across one or more graphic windows (see _shrink_u_expr).
408	    Multiple windows combine via max() (they don't overlap in time)."""
409	    corner_x, corner_y = POS[SHRINK_CORNER]
410	    u_terms = [_shrink_u_expr(gs, ge, td) for gs, ge in windows]
411	    u_expr = u_terms[0]
412	    for term in u_terms[1:]:
413	        u_expr = f"max({u_expr}\\,{term})"
414	    w_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_W}+({PIP_W}-{HERO_W})*{u_expr})/2))"
415	    h_expr = f"(2*round(({HERO_H}+({PIP_H}-{HERO_H})*{u_expr})/2))"
416	    x_expr = f"({HERO_X}+({corner_x}-{HERO_X})*{u_expr})"
417	    y_expr = f"({HERO_Y}+({corner_y}-{HERO_Y})*{u_expr})"
418	    return dict(w=w_expr, h=h_expr, x=x_expr, y=y_expr, u=u_expr)

422	    """Hero-stage webcam_primary layout: retrowave-loop background, the
423	    webcam feed enlarged to ~980px tall (its native 4:3 aspect preserved,
424	    never distorted) and centered, a neon border loop scaled/recentered to
425	    hug the new larger webcam box, and a subtle full-frame grain/flicker loop
426	    on top of it all. Ranges in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES additionally shrink the
427	    webcam+border aside into SHRINK_CORNER, eased, while that range's own
428	    graphic overlay(s) are on screen (see OVERLAYS[idx] + _hero_transform),
429	    holding there for the graphic's window before easing back to hero size.
430	    The rounded-corner mask (pip_mask.png) is scaled in lockstep with the
431	    webcam feed itself (same w/h expressions) so the corner radius scales
432	    proportionally with the box at every point in the animation, hero size,
433	    corner size, and everywhere in between.
434	    """
435	    dur = end - start
436	    overlays = OVERLAYS.get(idx)
437	    dynamic = idx in DYNAMIC_SHRINK_RANGES and overlays
438	
439	    bg_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-i", str(RETROWAVE_BG)]
440	    grain_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(GRAIN_LOOP)]
441	    border_args = ["-stream_loop", "-1", "-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-i", str(NEON_BORDER)]
442	    # -loop 1: pip_mask.png must be a continuously-supplied (infinite) frame
443	    # stream, not a single frame -- in the dynamic-shrink case its own
444	    # scale=...:eval=frame runs in lockstep with the webcam's per-frame w(t)/
445	    # h(t), and without -loop 1 the mask stream only ever provides ITS one
446	    # native frame, letting the mask's scale freeze at that single evaluation
447	    # while the webcam's own scale keeps re-evaluating every frame -- the
448	    # resulting size mismatch corrupts alphamerge (confirmed: produced a
449	    # solid dark rectangular artifact + ghosting mid-transition in range 5's
450	    # grow-back animation before this fix).
451	    # -framerate 60 alongside -loop 1: keeps the mask's own per-frame `t`
452	    # exactly in lockstep with the webcam's 60fps clock (image2's default
453	    # loop rate is 25fps, which would otherwise desync the two independent
454	    # eval=frame scale instances below just enough to size-mismatch them).
455	    mask_args = ["-loop", "1", "-framerate", "60", "-i", str(ASSETS / "pip_mask.png")]
456	    # Blank transparent canvas, full 1920x1080 frame size, used only in the
457	    # dynamic-shrink case (see below) as the fixed-size base that the
458	    # shrinking/growing webcam and mask each get overlaid onto. MUST be the
459	    # full frame (not just HERO_W x HERO_H) -- the corner box (bottom-right,
460	    # up to x=1880,y=1040) sits well outside the hero box's own footprint
461	    # (up to x=1613,y=1030), so a HERO_W x HERO_H canvas silently clips the
462	    # settled-corner content off its right/bottom edge (confirmed bug: ~46%
463	    # of the corner box's width was clipped, showing background bleed-through
464	    # -- see report).
465	    blank_args = ["-f", "lavfi", "-i", f"color=c=black@0.0:s=1920x1080:r=60"]
466	    # input indices: 0=screen(audio only) 1=webcam 2=retrowave bg 3=grain
467	    # 4=neon border 5=mask 6=blank canvas (dynamic ranges only)
468	    next_idx = 7 if dynamic else 6
469	
470	    # Grain/flicker loop composited onto the RAW retrowave background only,
471	    # before the neon border and webcam are drawn on top -- so the border and
472	    # webcam feed stay crisp/undegraded and the grain reads as texture on the
473	    # background plate itself, not a filter over the whole frame (previously
474	    # this was applied last, over the fully-assembled frame including the
475	    # webcam, so the grain visibly covered the presenter's face too -- fixed
476	    # by moving it here, ahead of the border/webcam compositing).
477	    filt = f"[2:v][3:v]overlay=x=0:y=0[bg_grain];"
478	
479	    if dynamic:
480	        windows = [(ov["rel_start"], ov["rel_start"] + ov["dur"]) for ov in overlays]
481	        tf = _hero_transform(windows)
482	        u = tf["u"]
483	        # alphamerge (and the final overlay) need CONSTANT frame dimensions
484	        # from both of their inputs at every frame -- feeding them a stream
485	        # whose eval=frame scale genuinely changes size frame-to-frame
486	        # errors out ("Invalid argument", confirmed by isolated repro; see

509	            f"[blankmask][wcmasks]overlay=x='{off_x}':y='{off_y}'[wcmask];"

511	            f"[4:v]split=2[nb1][nb2];"

529	            f"[bgb][wcr]overlay=x=0:y=0[with_wc];"
530	        )
531	    else:
532	        filt += (
533	            f"[1:v]scale={HERO_W}:{HERO_H}[wc];"
534	            f"[5:v]scale={HERO_W}:{HERO_H}[wcmask];"
535	            f"[wc][wcmask]alphamerge[wcr];"
536	            f"[4:v]scale=w='iw*{NEON_SCALE_HERO}':h='ih*{NEON_SCALE_HERO}',"
537	            f"crop=1920:1080:(iw-1920)/2:(ih-1080)/2[border_hero];"
538	            f"[bg_grain][border_hero]overlay=x=0:y=0[bgb];"
539	            f"[bgb][wcr]overlay=x={HERO_X}:y={HERO_Y}[with_wc];"
540	        )

543	    filt += f"[0:a]{afade(dur)}[a]"

1	"""Ken-Burns-style animated push-in zoom for a video segment, via ffmpeg's
2	zoompan filter. Import zoom_filter_string() from a compositing script, or run
3	this file directly to print/test one filter string.
4	
5	WHY THIS EXISTS (hard-won debugging, don't repeat it):
6	
7	1. ffmpeg's `crop` filter only evaluates its w/h expressions ONCE, at init.
8	   Only x/y support true per-frame animation. So you CANNOT animate a
9	   shrinking crop box with `crop=w='...':h='...'` and expect a smooth zoom --
10	   every frame gets the same (first-computed) w/h, only the position pans.
11	   `zoompan` is the correct filter for an actual animated zoom level; it has
12	   no such limitation.
13	
14	2. zoompan produces a visible "vibration"/jitter right as an ease-out curve
15	   flattens near its target (many consecutive frames end up with nearly-but-
16	   not-exactly-identical zoom values, and the resulting crop window's
17	   pixel-rounded position dithers by +/-1px at the sampling resolution).
18	   Fix, both required: (a) pre-scale the source 2x before zoompan so that
19	   same 1px dither becomes a sub-pixel error at output res, and (b) round
20	   the zoom expression to a fixed precision so floating-point noise near the
21	   plateau can't produce distinct-but-nearly-equal values frame to frame.
22	
23	3. When composing the rounding fix as a string template, WRAP THE WHOLE
24	   INNER EXPRESSION IN PARENTHESES before multiplying: `round((expr)*2000)`,
25	   not `round(expr*2000)`. ffmpeg's expression parser applies its own
26	   operator precedence to the resulting string -- multiplication binds
27	   tighter than the addition inside `expr` (which is `1 + (...)`), so without
28	   the parens only the last multiplicative term gets scaled, collapsing the
29	   whole zoom range down near 0 and silently producing NO visible zoom at
30	   all (still renders successfully, wrong output, easy to ship by accident --
31	   always pull a before/after frame and confirm the crop actually changed
32	   size, don't just check the ffmpeg command exits 0).
33	
34	4. ffmpeg eval expressions have no `clip(x,lo,hi)` function -- use
35	   `min(max(x,lo),hi)`.
36	"""
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	
40	def zoom_filter_string(
41	    rs: float,
42	    rd: float,
43	    cx: float,
44	    cy: float,
45	    zoom: float,
46	    out_rs: float | None = None,
47	    out_rd: float | None = None,
48	    fps: int = 60,
49	    out_w: int = 1920,
50	    out_h: int = 1080,
51	    supersample: int = 2,
52	) -> str:
53	    """Build a zoompan-based push-in filter string.
54	
55	    rs, rd: ramp-in start / duration, in seconds RELATIVE TO THIS SEGMENT'S
56	        OWN START (i.e. seconds into the extracted clip, not absolute source
57	        time).
58	    cx, cy: target crop center, in ORIGINAL (1x, out_w x out_h) source pixel
59	        coordinates -- e.g. (955, 650) for a point at x=955,y=650 in a
60	        1920x1080 frame. Internally scaled by `supersample`.
61	    zoom: target zoom factor (e.g. 2.0 = crop window is half the frame's
62	        width/height, centered on cx,cy). Keep this <= ~2.2x in practice --
63	        much beyond that visibly softens the image since you're cropping a
64	        smaller and smaller fraction of the source's native resolution.
65	    out_rs, out_rd: optional ramp-OUT start/duration (relative, same
66	        convention as rs/rd) if the zoom should release back to full-frame
67	        before the segment ends. Omit (None) to hold at target zoom through
68	        the end of the segment -- appropriate when a cut immediately follows.
69	    """
70	    rsf, rdf = rs * fps, rd * fps
71	    cx_s, cy_s = cx * supersample, cy * supersample
72	    in_ease = f"(1-pow(1-min(max((on-{rsf})/{rdf}\\,0)\\,1)\\,3))"
73	    if out_rs is not None:
74	        orsf, ordf = out_rs * fps, out_rd * fps
75	        out_ease = f"(1-min(max((on-{orsf})/{ordf}\\,0)\\,1))"
76	        raw_zoom = f"1+({zoom}-1)*{in_ease}*{out_ease}"
77	    else:
78	        raw_zoom = f"1+({zoom}-1)*{in_ease}"
79	    # NOTE the parens around raw_zoom -- see docstring point 3. Don't remove them.
80	    zoom_expr = f"round(({raw_zoom})*2000)/2000"
